tagline: Where the Asian shore meets the Black Sea — forest villages, Ottoman summer palaces, and some of Istanbul's most scenic and untouched coastline.

items.name: Anadolu Kavağı Çay Bahçeleri
items.description: Tea gardens in the fishing village of Anadolu Kavağı at the very mouth of the Bosphorus. An extraordinary setting at the end of the ferry line.
items.tip: Take the full Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü — the journey is as spectacular as the destination.

items.name: Polonezköy Café
items.description: The Polish village of Polonezköy in the Beykoz forests has charming garden cafés serving breakfast and tea in a completely different Istanbul atmosphere.

items.name: Anadolu Kavağı Balık Restoranları
items.description: A row of fish restaurants in the village where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Some of Istanbul's most memorable fish meals with extraordinary views.
items.tip: Order the grilled Black Sea fish — species you won't find elsewhere in the city. The village is the journey's reward.

items.name: Polonezköy Restoranları
items.description: Forest restaurants in the historic Polish village serving traditional Turkish and European cuisine in garden settings. A unique lunch destination.

items.name: Yoros Kalesi
items.description: A ruined Genoese-Byzantine castle on the hill above Anadolu Kavağı with what may be the greatest panoramic view in all of Istanbul — both continents visible.
items.tip: The climb from the village takes 25-30 minutes. Go in the morning before the ferry day-trippers arrive.

items.name: Polonezköy Nature Park
items.description: A forested national park around the historic Polish village. Excellent walking trails, picnic areas, and complete escape from the city.

items.name: Bosphorus Ferry (Eminönü–Anadolu Kavağı)
items.description: The full Bosphorus round trip — arguably the greatest urban boat journey in the world, stopping at both shores all the way to the Black Sea entrance.
items.tip: The ferry runs twice daily (morning and midday departures). Buy your return ticket on arrival — the last ferry fills up fast.

tips: Beykoz is far from the metro — best reached by ferry (Anadolu Kavağı line from Eminönü) or by bus from Üsküdar.
The Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavağı is one of Istanbul's unmissable experiences — take the full trip at least once.
Polonezköy is best visited on weekdays; it gets crowded with Istanbul families on weekends.
Mobile signal can be unreliable in the forest areas — download maps offline before visiting.
